config.title: Travelling Alone in Berlin - FAQ
config.subtitle: Straight answers for giving a solo Berlin day enough shape without over-planning it.

items.q: How should I plan one day alone in Berlin?
items.a: Choose one part of Berlin first, give one real place the middle of the day and finish nearby. Use Alexanderplatz and Museum Island for a historic-centre day, Tiergarten for a quieter day, or Kottbusser Tor and Markthalle Neun for a Kreuzberg day when the current schedule fits.

items.q: Is Museum Island a good solo Berlin stop?
items.a: Yes, when you want architecture, museum context and a compact central area. Check the individual museum's current opening hours, admission and access information before fixing a ticket or time slot.

items.q: Is a Berlin free walking tour good for solo travellers?
items.a: It can be a useful first move when conversation and historic context are what you are missing. BerlinWalk starts at the World Clock on Alexanderplatz and lasts about 2 hours through the historic centre of former East Berlin, then you can continue alone.

items.q: Should I combine Tiergarten with Museum Island in one day?
items.a: Treat them as two different day shapes first. If one place is giving you a good pace, stay with it instead of crossing the city to complete a list. Check the live BVG connection search before moving.

items.q: How do I use Berlin public transport while travelling alone?
items.a: Use the BVG connection search shortly before leaving each place, check disruptions and the return journey, and avoid adding a long cross-city move just because a saved pin is technically reachable.
